newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI COASTS TO FLAT FINISH IN MIXED TONE.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI COASTS TO FLAT FINISH IN MIXED TONE.

text.p: Shares recovered from early
weakness, but ended little changed on Tuesday after fair-volume
trade, with sentiment mixed amid Europe-wide jitters over the
future of monetary union, brokers said.
The FOX futures index dipped 0.06 percent to 1,065.45,
while the all-share HEX index scraped up a 0.12 percent gain to
3,085.22 points.
Nokia ended a steady session off slightly, shedding 0.50
markka to 346.00, in moderate 150 million markka volume.
Amer retreated sharply from Monday's gains, ending down
7.50 markka at 100.00.
That was still a markka below where the share had traded
ahead of Monday's news that Jonathan Bryan Guinness, Lord
Moyne, had acquired a controlling stake in the company.
That news initially sent the share to new year highs before
doubts set in about the new owner's intentions. "Amer is a
question mark," one broker said.
Rebounding from early loses, Partek gained 2.10 markka to
close at 96.00 in hefty 75 million markka trade.
The focus is now on a slate of Finnish interim reports due
this week and next, including results from Valmet on
Wednesday and Outokumpu on Thursday, brokers said.
The median of analysts' forecasts for Valmet's
January-April profit in a Reuters poll had been for earnings of
358 million markka.
Brokers said the market would also be watching the U.S.
jobless data on Friday, still on edge for any hint of the U.S.
Fed's next monetary policy move.
